FilePicker

The FilePicker control allows users to browse for a file or directory. It keeps its own current directory, so using the picker does not change the working directory of your application.

Properties and Methods

  • SelectionMode: Controls whether users can select a File, Directory, or FileOrDirectory.
  • Extensions: A case-insensitive set of file extensions, including the dot. An empty set allows all files. Call Refresh after changing the filter.
  • NavigateTo / Refresh / NavigateToParent: Changes or refreshes the directory being browsed. These return whether the operation succeeded; ErrorMessage describes a failure.
  • Path / CurrentDirectory / SelectedEntry: Path is the last confirmed selection. CurrentDirectory is the folder being browsed, and SelectedEntry is the highlighted item. Setting Path does not navigate.
  • SelectionConfirmed / Cancelled: SelectionConfirmed receives the selected path. Cancelled is a parameterless event for closing or handling cancellation.
  • OnFileSelected / OnDirectorySelected: Parameterless callback properties. Read Path from the picker to get the selection.

Keyboard Controls

  • Enter / Right: Open a directory; Enter confirms a file.
  • Space / F2: Select a directory / the current directory when the mode permits it.
  • Backspace / Left, F5: Go up / refresh.
  • Up / Down, Home / End, Page keys: Navigate the list; typing cycles matching prefixes.

Notes

sampleDirectory is a path provided by your application. This example uses a temporary directory containing Layout.mxml and a Pages folder. The displayed path is shortened to /demo in the output example.

The MXML example uses a factory to set the starting directory and extension filter before the control is created.

Directory enumeration is synchronous. If you need to browse slow, remote or very large directories, you should provide your own asynchronous loading UI. FilePicker is not a filesystem permission boundary.

The common position, color, visibility and lifetime settings are inherited from UIElement. While attached to a running window, update the control on the UI thread.
